# zerops_project_dedicated_ipv4 (Resource)

Requests or adopts a billed dedicated project IPv4 address. Destroy only removes Terraform ownership: the address remains billed until its project is deleted. A shared IPv4 flag is not a dedicated allocation.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# This allocation is billed. Destroying this resource only forgets ownership;
# the address remains allocated and billed until the owning project is deleted.
# An existing allocation is adopted without requesting another address.
resource "zerops_project_dedicated_ipv4" "example" {
  project_id = zerops_project.example.id

  timeouts {
    create = "30m"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `project_id` (String) Project to adopt or allocate an IPv4 address for. Only one resource may own the allocation.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) Operation timeouts. One timeout covers lock acquisition, API requests, queued work and readiness polling. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `address` (String) Dedicated IPv4 address returned by the project API.
- `id` (String) Project ID.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import only adopts an existing allocation; it never requests an address.
terraform import zerops_project_dedicated_ipv4.example PROJECT_ID
```
